exposure: Women with one previous CS, pregnant of a singleton in cephalic presentation, delivering after 37 weeks 0 days
Counselling with a decision aid (DA) including a prediction model on VBAC
finding: Counselling with a DA did not significantly affect VBAC rates but was associated with a reduction in unplanned CS rates, an increase in elective repeat CS rates, and improved patient involvement in decision-making.
mod_finding: The study compared counseling with a decision aid for women with one previous cesarean section and found no difference in vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) rates, but an increase in elective repeat cesarean sections and a decrease in unplanned cesarean sections.
